title: Add per-class scheduler metrics + tracing (short/long queues) and dashboard requirements
creator: Lena Fischer
description:
Goal
Add production-safe metrics and traces to evaluate the mixed-workload scheduler prototype (short/long request classes) and support canary rollback decisions. This ticket defines metric names + labels, implements instrumentation in runtime, and aligns dashboard + alert requirements with Observability (Allison Grant) and SRE (Aisha Bello / Sean Gallagher).

Context
The two-queue/class-based scheduler reduces head-of-line blocking in mixed prompt-length distributions, but we need per-class visibility to prove p95 improvements and to detect starvation/fairness regressions during canary.

Owners / collaborators
- Eng (runtime instrumentation): Julian Moore (assignee)
- Observability standards + dashboards: Allison Grant
- Telemetry pipeline support: Logan Wright (as needed for aggregation/histograms)
- SRE consumers: Aisha Bello, Sean Gallagher

Scope
1) Metrics (Prometheus/OpenTelemetry)
We will add per-class scheduler metrics with low-cardinality labels. Classes are a bounded enum: {short,long}.

Naming conventions
- Prefix: runtime_scheduler_
- Avoid request_id/prompt_hash/customer_id labels (cardinality risk).
- Allowed labels: class, pool, model, region, result (success|dropped|rejected), reason (bounded enum), stage (prefill|decode where applicable).

Required metrics (new)
A. Queue depth + wait time
1) runtime_scheduler_queue_depth
- Type: gauge
- Labels: class, pool, model, region
- Semantics: number of requests currently enqueued (not including in-flight).

2) runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Labels: class, pool, model, region
- Measurement: time from enqueue -> first dispatch attempt (prefill dispatch) and time from enqueue -> first token (TTFT proxy) where feasible.
- Note: if we can’t reliably measure enqueue->TTFT inside runtime, we still emit enqueue->dispatch and rely on API layer TTFT. If we do emit TTFT-like, ensure it’s clearly named and documented.

B. Dispatch share + token budgeting
3) runtime_scheduler_dispatch_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: class, pool, model, region, stage (prefill|decode)
- Semantics: increments on every dispatch decision where work is assigned to the batch builder.

4) runtime_scheduler_tokens_dispatched_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: class, pool, model, region, stage
- Semantics: token budget consumed/assigned by scheduler per iteration (approximate; doc the exact counting method).

5) runtime_scheduler_token_budget_overrun_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: class, pool, model, region, stage
- Semantics: increments when configured per-iteration budget would be exceeded and guardrail logic triggers (e.g., clamp/defer).

C. Starvation / aging guardrails
6) runtime_scheduler_starvation_events_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: class, pool, model, region, reason
- reason enum (bounded): exceeded_max_wait, exceeded_max_skew, forced_dispatch, aging_boost_applied

7) runtime_scheduler_max_queue_wait_seconds
- Type: gauge
- Labels: class, pool, model, region
- Semantics: max observed time-in-queue in the last scrape interval (or since process start if that’s what we can do cheaply). Document behavior.

D. Class-level latency (runtime internal)
8) runtime_scheduler_prefill_latency_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Labels: class, pool, model, region
- Semantics: time spent in prefill compute (GPU time is ideal but wall-clock acceptable; document).

9) runtime_scheduler_decode_iteration_latency_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Labels: class, pool, model, region
- Semantics: per-iteration decode scheduling/dispatch overhead (not model compute). Helps catch scheduler thrash/regressions.

E. Drop / reject visibility (coupling to backpressure)
10) runtime_scheduler_rejections_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: class, pool, model, region, reason
- reason enum: queue_full, max_concurrency, deadline_exceeded, backpressure_upstream

2) Tracing
We will add trace spans/events on the request lifecycle with class annotations.

Trace requirements
- Span: scheduler.enqueue (attributes: class, pool, model, region, input_tokens_bucket)
- Span: scheduler.dispatch (attributes: class, stage, queue_depth_short, queue_depth_long, policy_version, token_budget_short, token_budget_long)
- Event: scheduler.aging_applied (attributes: class, age_ms)
- Event: scheduler.token_budget_clamped (attributes: class, stage, requested_tokens, allowed_tokens)

Sampling
- Default: very low sampling in prod (e.g., 0.1% or “errors only”), higher in canary/perf environments via config.
- Ensure spans do not attach large payloads (no prompt text, no token arrays).

3) Dashboard requirements (hand-off / alignment with Allison)
We need a per-pool view and a global rollup. Minimum panels:
- Queue depth (short vs long) over time, per pool
- p50/p95 queue_wait_seconds (short vs long)
- Dispatch share (% short vs long) and tokens_dispatched share (%), stacked
- Starvation events (rate) split by class/reason
- Rejections rate split by class/reason
- Prefill latency histogram p50/p95 (short vs long)
- Canary comparison: “scheduler_policy=baseline vs mixed_v1” overlay where possible (if policy version label exists; otherwise split by pool)

Alert requirements (SRE)
- Starvation events > threshold for 10m (class=long especially)
- Max queue wait > N seconds for 5m (per class)
- Rejections spike (rate increase + sustained)
- Queue depth saturation (depth rising monotonically + wait p95 rising)

Non-goals
- Customer-specific QoS metrics or multi-tenant tier labeling (prototype only).
- High-cardinality per-route/per-request labels.

Implementation notes
- Metrics should live in the scheduler module and be emitted at the decision points (enqueue, dequeue/dispatch, forced dispatch/aging, budget clamp, reject).
- Keep hot-path overhead minimal (pre-allocate label handles; avoid string formatting on every tick).
- If adding histograms, use existing runtime metrics primitives and confirm bucket strategy with Observability (avoid too many buckets per label set).

Acceptance criteria
- All metrics above present in staging and in perf-canary runs.
- Labels conform to bounded enums; no high-cardinality values.
- Dashboard spec finalized with Allison; Grafana dashboard created or updated by Observability with the agreed panels.
- Runbook references: link to dashboard + which panels to watch during canary.

Links

- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/scheduler-class-metrics-dashboard-spec.json

comments: 2025-12-08 (Julian Moore): Drafted metric list + labels; set up quick review with Allison to sanity check naming + histogram buckets. Key decision: keep labels limited to {class,pool,model,region,stage,reason} and avoid route/customer labels.

2025-12-10 (Allison Grant): Looks good overall. Two requests: (1) document exact semantics for queue_wait (enqueue->first dispatch vs enqueue->first token) because teams will misread it; (2) keep histogram bucket count small to avoid TS explosion when multiplied by pool/model/region.

2025-12-11 (Julian Moore): Implemented counters/gauges in scheduler hot path with pre-registered label sets. Added starvation_events_total and token_budget_overrun_total to make canary rollback decisions easier (these should stay near zero).

2025-12-13 (Aisha Bello): For canary, we want an explicit long-class starvation signal. Please ensure starvation_events_total has a clear reason enum and that max_queue_wait_seconds is available per class (panel + alert).

2025-12-16 (Julian Moore): Opened PR for per-class metrics + trace events. Added policy_version attribute on trace dispatch span (not a metric label) to avoid cardinality issues but still enable debugging in traces.

2025-12-18 (Logan Wright): Confirmed the runtime metrics backend supports these histograms; recommended bucket set: [0.001,0.005,0.01,0.025,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1,2.5,5,10]. Anything beyond 10s should be a separate alert on max_queue_wait_seconds.

2025-12-19 (Julian Moore): Marking In Review pending final approval from Allison on dashboard panel mapping + SRE sign-off on alert thresholds for canary. Once merged, will update runbook with dashboard link + panel checklist.
